entries.proposition: Both patients were treated in open-label single-patient studies with no concurrent control.
entries.snippet: Open-label, first-in-human, investigational individualized allele-selective ASO therapy demonstrates positive safety and efficacy in two patients with different causal GOF and mixed GOF/LOF SCN2A variants and phenotypes

entries.proposition: The predefined primary endpoint was the change in the countable motor seizure frequency at 12 and 24 months, analysed per patient with a generalised linear model.
entries.snippet: For both patients, primary endpoints were predefined as the change from baseline in countable motor seizure frequency at 12 and 24 months after ASO administration.

entries.proposition: Patient 1 pre-treatment recording lasted 90 days; patient 2 only 42 days.
entries.snippet: Patient 1’s seizures were recorded consecutively for 90 days in the pre-ASO period and 744 days in the post-ASO period.

entries.proposition: Patient 2 baseline recording lasted 42 days against 480 days after.
entries.snippet: Patient 2’s seizures were recorded consecutively for 42 days in the pre-ASO period and 480 days in the post-ASO period.

entries.proposition: Patient 1 prespecified seizure test was not significant.
entries.snippet: The treatment effect was not statistically significant (β = −0.298, 95% CI = −0.846 to 0.249, P = 0.286).

entries.proposition: Patient 2 prespecified seizure test reported an estimated 90 percent reduction.
entries.snippet: Seizures after initiation of ASO were significantly reduced by an estimated 90% in prespecified statistical analysis (β = −2.338, 95% CI = −3.021 to −1.655, P < 0.001).

entries.proposition: In patient 2 a higher dose level went with slightly more seizures in the model.
entries.snippet: higher ASO dosing was associated with slightly increased seizures compared to lower ASO doses for this patient

entries.proposition: The protocols were amended during treatment, regulator-driven, and endpoints were added after improvement.
entries.snippet: Later amendments incorporated additional outcome measures due to patient improvement and developmental skills gained (including gait).

entries.proposition: For patient 2, early amendments expanded the primary endpoints beyond seizures to motor and gastrointestinal domains.
entries.snippet: For Patient 2, additional early amendments expanded the primary endpoints beyond seizure frequency to include assessments of motor and gastrointestinal domains.

entries.proposition: The authors acknowledge that the minimal clinically important difference is difficult to define in n-of-1 settings and rely on predefined individualised goals.
entries.snippet: These n = 1 trials required predefined individualized treatment goals to assess meaningful change based on the concept of the minimal clinically important difference (MCID), the smallest response considered clinically impactful

entries.proposition: Neurodevelopmental success was defined as exceeding the child's own baseline annual rate of gain, with pretreatment windows of 14 months or only 4 months, and none for one domain.
entries.snippet: Fourteen months of pretreatment data were used for cognitive and expressive language subscales; four months of pretreatment data were used for fine and gross motor subscales. No pretreatment data were available for the receptive language subscale.

entries.proposition: The authors write that the children met prespecified outcomes by exceeding their baseline annual rates of gain.
entries.snippet: Patients met prespecified outcomes by exceeding baseline annual rates of gain after treatment with ASOs.

entries.proposition: The Discussion states a disease-modifying effect from the open-label results.
entries.snippet: improvement in neurodevelopmental outcomes with disease-modifying effect, offering an alternative treatment paradigm

entries.proposition: The authors state that long-term follow-up will inform durability.
entries.snippet: Long-term follow-up will further inform the durability of safety and efficacy findings.

entries.proposition: No ASO-related serious adverse events; table lists events including a possibly related tic and a fall attributed to patient 3 in a two-patient study.
entries.snippet: No ASO-related adverse events or serious adverse events were reported in either patient (Table 2).

entries.proposition: Table 2 lists an adverse event for a patient labelled 3 in a study of two patients.
entries.snippet: Fall | 3 | Moderate | No | No | No

entries.proposition: Design pre-clinical gating in patient-derived neurons: allele selectivity by IC50 for each ASO.
entries.snippet: the ASO demonstrated 42-fold selectivity in patient 1 and 53-fold selectivity in patient 2, based on IC50 values for mutant versus wild-type transcripts.

entries.proposition: Time to access: regulator research IND and institutional approval for patient 1 within months.
entries.snippet: Rush University IRB approval was received under compassionate use in May 2023, and consent and enrollment occurred in June 2023

entries.proposition: A separate cohort analysis found 3 of 19 patients had a compatible SNP configuration.
entries.snippet: Sixteen percent (that is, three patients) in our cohort were identified as having the correct SNP configuration amenable to treatment with the same ASO initially designed for Patient 2

entries.proposition: Fig 1: patient 1 daily seizure average was 2.2 before and between 1.3 and 2.8 across later dosing intervals; patient 2 was 2.0 before, 4.6 around a coronavirus infection at the start, 1.3 to 1.4 early, 4.1 and 3.1 in two later intervals and 0 in the last interval; the percentage of seizure-free days in patient 2 varied from about 3 to about 98 percent across visits.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1a interval averages above the bars: prestudy 2.2, then 1.3, 1.6, 1.4, 2.2, 2.0, 2.2, 2.8, 1.3, 1.8, 1.9, 1.3; green line phenytoin level falling from about 28 to about 7 across the first 170 days. Fig 1b: prestudy 2.0; 4.6 (spike near a labelled coronavirus infection at day 1); 1.3; 1.4; 1.4; 4.1; 3.1; 0 in the last interval. Fig 1c: percent of days without seizures about 3 prestudy and about 47, 65, 33, 58, 12, 46 and 98 at days 21, 77, 168, 253, 336, 434 and 490.

entries.proposition: Fig 2: patient 1 annualised gain in the cognitive subscale was lower after treatment than before (about 10 against 3), the receptive-language and expressive-language gains at 18 months were smaller at 24 months, and communication T-score changes are shown for both patients.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 2a annualised change in growth scale value: cognitive about 10 pretreatment and 3 at 24 months; expressive language none pre and about 4 post; receptive language about 10 post with no pretreatment bar; fine motor about -6 pre and 3 post; gross motor about -12 pre and 7 post. Fig 2b change from baseline for receptive language about 25 at 18 months and 20 at 24 months; expressive about 12 then 8. Fig 2c-d ORCA T-score changes; Fig 2e D-FIS total 43 at baseline, 29 at 6 months and 26 at 12 months for patient 2.

entries.proposition: Fig 3: patient 1 behaviour scale scores were already similar at pre-treatment and baseline and fell after treatment; hyperactivity rose again between 12 and 24 months.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 3a RBS-R: irritability 17 pretreatment, 18 baseline, about 1 at 12 and at 24 months; stereotypic behaviour 11, 11, 7, 4; hyperactivity/noncompliance 25, 26, 10, 15. Fig 3b stereotypic 9, 11, 4, 7 and self-injurious 7, 8, 2 and no 24-month bar. Fig 3c sensory profile total scores near the maximum at pretreatment and baseline and near the normal line at 12 and 24 months.

entries.proposition: Fig 4: the panel labelled change from baseline equals the 12-month value minus the pretreatment value, not the baseline value; the large domestic and community declines and the fine-motor gain largely occurred between the pretreatment and baseline assessments, before any dose.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 4b raw scores pretreatment/baseline/12 months: domestic about 38/10/10, community 36/10/10, fine motor 37/53/57, receptive 66/64/67, interpersonal 63/59/65; Fig 4a bars (captioned change from baseline): domestic about -28, community -26, fine motor +20, receptive +1, interpersonal +2 - each equal to the 12-month value minus the pretreatment value. Fig 4e ABC-C pretreatment/baseline/12 months: irritability 27/23/17, social withdrawal 11/5/1, stereotypy 12/7/3, hyperactivity 31/20/20. Fig 4c-d Bristol stool ratings mostly 5 throughout with a sustained 5 and fewer 6 to 7 ratings after about day 77.
